prompt_md: Two lengths are each uniformly random between 0 and 10 m. Rounding each to the nearest meter then adding, or adding then rounding: chance both give the same number?
prompt_short: Round then add, or add then round. Chance they agree?
hint_md: Look at the two rounding errors.
explain_intuition_md: Each rounding error is anywhere from minus half a meter to plus half a meter. The two methods agree only when the errors do not add up to more than half a meter in either direction, and they do so a quarter of the time. Rounding feels harmless, so 100% is tempting.
explain_math_md: With errors $e_1, e_2$ uniform on $[-\tfrac12, \tfrac12]$, the results agree iff $|e_1 + e_2| < \tfrac12$: $$P = 1 - 2 \cdot \tfrac12 \left(\tfrac12\right)^2 = \tfrac34$$
